editorial:
Imagine being a worldwide pop star about to launch a massive tour, only to start seeing things that are not really there. That is the nightmare Skye Riley faces in this follow-up. The story throws you into her glamorous but stressful life, where every smile hides something dark. You feel the pressure of fame pressing down on her as strange and scary events keep piling up. The movie mixes flashy concert scenes with quiet, creepy moments, so you never quite know what is real. It keeps you guessing while pulling you deeper into Skye's world.

The acting really sells the fear, especially in the big emotional scenes. The pacing moves fast and rarely lets you breathe, which works well for horror fans. On the downside, some scares feel familiar if you watched the first film, and a few plot points get confusing near the end. Still, if you enjoy psychological horror with a music twist, this one is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Skye realizes the curse has fully taken hold. She tries to fight it but cannot escape. The twist reveals that the smiling entity has been controlling her all along, and she ends up passing the curse to a massive crowd during a live performance. The movie ends with thousands of people smiling at once, suggesting the horror will spread far beyond her. It is a bleak, shocking finish that leaves you stunned.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological horror and creepy thrillers.
